references.text: Parallel text regarding the peace offering of cattle, describing the same fat that covers the entrails and all the fat on the entrails
Parallel text regarding the peace offering of small livestock (sheep), with the same description of the fat to be offered to the Lord
Sin offering with the same instructions concerning the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat on the entrails
The thank offering laws repeat the instructions about the fat that covers the entrails
The consecration offering for the priests includes the fat that covers the entrails; the same terminology is used
The prohibition against eating fat from animals offered as a burnt offering to the Lord
A clear parallel showing the standardization of how fat is handled in various forms of peace offerings.
Highlights the theological unity that the fat always belongs to the Lord, regardless of the type of sacrifice.
Complementary text that completes the list of which pieces of fat are to be offered.
Confirms that the rule about the fat applies across different categories of sacrifices, including the Day of Atonement.
Demonstrates theological consistency in the handling of fat across peace offerings and sin offerings.
